audit.whatIsWrong: Rated TRICKY at 7.5/10 with Levels 1, 2 and 3 all given to Sett, while the page's own prose says 'Sett has no gap-closer until 6, so your Q is the whole early game' and the Level 1-2 spike card is a Malphite spike. Win rate is 54.96% Malphite over 1301 games.
audit.why: Both statements cannot be true. Seismic Shard is 625 range on 8s against a champion whose longest reach before 6 is Facebreaker at 490, and whose stun on that ability is conditional.
audit.corrected: Levels 1-2 are Malphite's while Sett has no way in; the lane tilts to Sett only as Grit and Knuckle Down's max-health damage come online, and again at two-plus items.

audit.whatIsWrong: The Level 6 spike claims 'Unstoppable Force beats his R suppress on range and travel time' without a number, and the 2+ item spike blames 'grit-stacking' rather than the ability that actually scales against a tank.
audit.why: Unstoppable Force is 1000 range on 130/115/100s; The Show Stopper is 400 range on 120/100/80s. Knuckle Down deals bonus damage 'based off of the target's max health' — that is what makes Sett's late scaling ugly for a health-stacking Malphite, not Grit.
audit.corrected: 1000 range against 400 at Level 6, and Knuckle Down's max-health damage is why buying HP makes his trades better.

audit.whatIsWrong: Two decisive conditions are stated as unconditional. (a) 'E grab-stun' appears five times — Facebreaker only stuns if there are enemies on opposite sides of Sett; alone on one side you are slowed, not stunned. (b) 'his W is true damage, armor won't reduce it' — Haymaker is true damage in the CENTRE of the punch and physical damage on the sides.
audit.why: Riot text, Facebreaker: 'Sett pulls in all enemies on opposite sides of him... If enemies were only on one side, they are slowed instead of stunned.' Haymaker: 'punch an area, dealing true damage in the center and physical damage on the sides.'
audit.corrected: Keep your back clear of the wave and Facebreaker is a slow, not a stun. If you have to eat Haymaker, eat it off-centre where your armour still applies.

audit.why: Pit Grit gives Sett health regeneration scaling off missing health, so the itemization line's anti-heal note is justified.

edits.before: Sett has no gap-closer until 6, so your Q (Seismic Shard) is the whole early game — open every approach with it to slow him and steal his move speed, and his E grab-stun can never line up. Granite Shield refreshes whenever you step out, so you eat his passive double-punch poke and reset the buffer for free. Don't auto-trade into a full W bar — let him waste the stored damage on minions, last-hit at Q range, and deny him the grit stacks his early game lives on.
edits.after: Sett has no gap-closer until 6, so Seismic Shard is the whole early game — open every approach with it to steal his move speed. And learn what Facebreaker (E, 16s) actually does: it stuns only if there are enemies on opposite sides of him, so with nothing behind you it is a slow. Never fight with the wave at your back. Granite Shield refreshes whenever you step out, and every point of poke you take feeds the Grit that loads Haymaker.

edits.before: Levels 4-5 you stabilize as Thunderclap (bonus armor + AoE empowered autos) and Ground Slam come online — E his attack speed down and your W autos out-sustain his double-punch. Level 6 is a genuine coin-flip because his R suppress slam and your R both want to commit first; your Unstoppable Force has the range and the knock-up, so if you can flank or catch him mid-W animation you win the exchange, but if he lands E into R first you're the one suppressed. Respect his stored W — never all-in while his bar is full.
edits.after: Levels 4-5 you stabilize as Thunderclap and Ground Slam come online — slow his attack speed and out-sustain the double punch. Haymaker deals true damage only in the centre of the punch; the sides are physical, so if you have to eat it, eat it off-centre where your armour still counts. Level 6 is a genuine coin-flip: Unstoppable Force reaches 1000 against The Show Stopper's 400, so you commit first or not at all. Never all-in into a full Grit bar, and never let his poke fill it for free while you sit in the wave.

edits.before: Sett has no dash and your Q steals his move speed the moment he steps up — he cannot land E to start a fight and just eats poke while Granite Shield refreshes.
edits.after: Sett has no dash and Seismic Shard steals his move speed as he steps up — and Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides of him, so keep your back clear.

edits.before: His W bar is now a real threat — a full smash deals true damage your armor can't soften, so this stage is genuinely even on who commits first.
edits.after: Haymaker is a real threat now, but only its centre is true damage — the sides are physical, so off-centre your armour still does its job.

edits.before: His W smash deals true damage straight through your armor and his grit brawl outscales a low-economy tank — stop dueling and play R for your carries.
edits.after: Knuckle Down (Q) scales off your max health and Haymaker's centre is true damage — a big HP bar is a liability, so play R for your carries instead.

edits.before: His stacked W true-damage smash and grit-stacking outscale a low-economy tank's armor — his strongest fight window, not yours.
edits.after: Knuckle Down (Q) takes a share of your max health and Haymaker's centre is true damage — the more HP you buy, the better he trades.

edits.before: Land E grab-stun to pin you, then W-smash the stored true damage you can't armor through
edits.after: Catch you with minions on his far side, so Facebreaker (E) stuns instead of only slowing

edits.before: Build armor — his W is true damage, don’t feed grit. Malphite wins the Haymaker cooldown windows.
edits.after: Build armour, don't feed Grit — Haymaker is true damage dead centre, physical on the sides.

edits.before: - Sett Haymaker: matchup-defining — True damage — armor won’t reduce it. Bait it. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Haymaker (18/16.5/15/13.5/12s): true damage in the CENTRE only, physical on the sides — stand off-centre. - Facebreaker (16s): stuns only with enemies on both sides. - Unstoppable Force: 130s.

edits.before: True damage — armor won’t reduce it. Bait it. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: True damage in the centre only; the sides are physical. 18s at rank 1, so bait it.

edits.before: Stack armor vs his W true damage
Burning it for tiny value leaves you naked for its full cooldown.
edits.after: Only the centre ignores armour — off-centre, your armour still counts.

edits.before: Trading with your passive shield down — that shield IS your trade margin; without it you are paying full price.
edits.after: Facebreaker only stuns with enemies on both sides of him — keep your back clear and it is only a slow.

edits.before: Track Sett's Haymaker: True damage — armor won’t reduce it. Bait it. When it is down — R-W-E him.
edits.after: Haymaker is true damage in the centre only, physical on the sides. Facebreaker stuns only if flanked.

notes: Two conditional mechanics were being taught as unconditional, and both change how you stand in lane. Facebreaker stuns only when there are enemies on opposite sides of Sett — with the wave in front of you and nothing behind, it is a slow — and the page called it 'E grab-stun' five times. Haymaker's true damage is only the centre of the punch; the sides are physical, so 'armor won't reduce it' is wrong for most of the ability's area. Level-chart conflict I could NOT fix inside the length band: content win[0..2] and full phases[0..2].side all read 'Sett', but the page's own prose says Sett cannot reach you before 6 and the packet levelChart gives Levels 1-2 to Malphite; 'Sett' (4 chars) to 'Malphite' (8) is +100% and would be rejected. Those six fields need a manual flip. Also unasserted on purpose: Sett's R carries a 'grounding' flag in the kit file that Riot's description does not support, and Malphite's Q/E carry the same misfiring flag.
